slides.title: Everything is on your phone
bullets: Your phone is your character sheet, your evidence file, and your conscience — keep it on you all night.
The tabs across the top hold who you are, what you can say, your role, your clues, and your history with other guests.
When the main screen gives an instruction, it outranks whatever you were doing. Even gossip.
slides.braun_says: Everything you need tonight is on the device in your hand. I've put my entire evening on there — my guests, my secrets, my house. Do try not to drop it in the champagne.

slides.title: Who you are tonight
bullets: Tonight you are the person on your screen — their name, their job, their voice, their grudges.
Read your backstory and your 'say' lines; they're yours to perform, embellish, and weaponize.
Your secrets are real. Guard them like money, spend them like money.
slides.braun_says: I've taken the liberty of deciding who each of you really is. Some of you are exactly who you appear to be. The rest of you — well. That's rather the point of the evening.

slides.title: Not everyone here is a guest
bullets: Not everyone here is a simple guest — some of you belong to something larger, and it's on your Role tab.
Your faction tells you what you know, who you can trust, and what winning means for you tonight.
Keep it secret. The wrong person learning your role is how evenings like this go badly.
slides.braun_says: Every party has its little societies — the loyal, the desperate, the ones taking notes. Tonight, yours comes with instructions. Check your role in private. Then lie about it in public, as is traditional.

slides.title: Nine cards, hidden in the house
bullets: Nine clue cards are hidden through the house, one to a room, each waiting at a spot worth searching.
Scan a card and its evidence goes into your phone — permanently, and only for those who've scanned it.
Evidence can be planted, and evidence can be scrubbed. Trust the cards. Verify the cards.
slides.braun_says: I've hidden nine cards in this house, and I flatter myself they're hidden well. Everything my home witnessed tonight is on them. If anything should happen to me — and it won't — do read my house's testimony carefully.

slides.title: Scan the people you meet
bullets: Every guest wears a badge — scan the people you meet and they're added to your phone's records.
Scanning someone unlocks your history with them, and history is where motives live.
You can't question a person your phone hasn't met. Mingle like your verdict depends on it.
slides.braun_says: Introductions at my parties are mandatory and now, I'm pleased to say, electronic. Point your phone, collect my guests. I acquired most of them the same way — one favor at a time.

slides.title: How somebody goes to jail
bullets: Three trials tonight. At each one, the room accuses, the accused answer, and everyone votes.
At trial, the accused cannot lie — direct questions get true answers. Everywhere else, all bets are off.
Convictions are permanent, and the convicted lose their vote. Choose like it counts, because it does.
slides.braun_says: Should this evening require justice, it will be served the way I serve everything: publicly, dramatically, and in courses. Three trials. Whoever you convict stays convicted — so do be sure. Or be persuasive.

slides.title: First, let's get to know each other
bullets: First: drinks, introductions, and reconnaissance — meet at least three guests you don't know.
Scan badges, trade stories, and check your history with the people you meet.
Pay attention to who's where. Later tonight, 'where were you?' becomes the only question that matters.
slides.braun_says: Enough instruction — this is a party. Go. Meet each other. Learn names, trade lies, admire my house. I'll be circulating for a while yet, and then, as always, the study at nine. A host must count the silver.
